topicName: Azure Backup, Site Recovery (ASR), and Disaster Recovery Strategies
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Enterprise Business Continuity: Azure Backup, Site Recovery, and DR Strategies"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Designing a robust business continuity and disaster recovery (BCDR) plan is critical for modern cloud infrastructure. Microsoft Azure provides native services like Azure Backup and Azure Site Recovery (ASR) to protect workloads against regional outages, ransomware, and accidental data deletion."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Azure Backup vs. Azure Site Recovery (ASR)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before architecting a solution, it is essential to understand the distinct roles of Azure Backup and Azure Site Recovery:"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Azure Backup: Focuses on data protection and recovery. It takes point-in-time backups of files, folders, virtual machines, and databases. Used primarily for operational recovery (deletions, corruption)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Azure Site Recovery (ASR): Focuses on workload replication and high availability. It continuously replicates virtual machines from a primary site to a secondary region. Used primarily for disaster recovery (entire datacenter failures)."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Configuring Azure Backup for Virtual Machines"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"To protect an Azure Virtual Machine, you must first provision a Recovery Services Vault. You can automate this process and enable backup using Azure CLI commands."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"az backup vault create --resource-group \"rg-bcdr-prod\" --name \"rsv-backup-vault\" --location \"eastus\""},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the vault is created, associate a backup policy and enable protection on the target virtual machine:"},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"az backup protection enable-for-vm --resource-group \"rg-bcdr-prod\" --vault-name \"rsv-backup-vault\" --vm \"vm-workload-01\" --policy-name \"DefaultPolicy\""},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Implementing Disaster Recovery with Azure Site Recovery (ASR)"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Azure Site Recovery orchestrates replication, failover, and failback to ensure business continuity with minimal Recovery Point Objective (RPO) and Recovery Time Objective (RTO)."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Replication: Disks and data are continuously mirrored to a target Azure region."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Test Failover: Allows administrators to run disaster recovery drills without impacting production workloads."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Planned / Unplanned Failover: Shifts traffic and compute operations to the secondary region during an actual outage."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Best Practices for Enterprise Disaster Recovery Strategies"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Define RPO and RTO metrics clearly for every application tier before selecting a replication strategy."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Implement immutable vaults and soft-delete features in Azure Backup to mitigate ransomware threats."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Conduct quarterly disaster recovery failover tests to validate automation scripts and recovery runbooks."}]
